parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the subshell responsible for the peak at 0.738 MJ/mol in the spectrum of magnesium, and state how many electrons it represents.
parts.sample: The peak at 0.738 MJ/mol is the 3s subshell. It represents 2 electrons (magnesium is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s²).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The 1s peak of magnesium is at a higher binding energy than the 1s peak of sodium. Explain why, in terms of Coulomb's law.

rubric.point: Mg has more protons (12 vs 11) and its 1s electrons are at about the same distance, so they are attracted more strongly
accept: greater nuclear charge, same shell/distance, stronger attraction

parts.sample: Magnesium has 12 protons and sodium 11. The 1s electrons of both are in the first shell, about the same distance from the nucleus, with no electrons shielding them. By Coulomb's law, the greater nuclear charge of Mg attracts its 1s electrons more strongly, so more energy is needed to remove them.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Aluminum has 13 electrons. Describe how its spectrum would differ from that of magnesium: state where any new peak would appear and its relative height.

rubric.point: A new peak for 3p, of relative height 1, at a lower binding energy than the 3s peak (the far right of the spectrum)
accept: a new 3p peak with one electron, to the right of 3s

parts.sample: Aluminum, [Ne] 3s² 3p¹, has one more subshell than magnesium. Its spectrum shows a new peak for the 3p electron, with a relative height of 1, at a lower binding energy than its 3s peak, at the far right of the spectrum. (The other peaks shift to slightly higher binding energies.)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The first ionization energy of aluminum is lower than that of magnesium. Explain why, using the electron configurations of both atoms.

rubric.point: The electron removed from Al is a 3p electron, higher in energy (held less tightly) than the 3s electron removed from Mg, partly shielded by the 3s electrons
accept: Al loses a 3p electron; Mg loses a 3s electron, which is held more tightly

parts.sample: Magnesium (1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s²) loses a 3s electron, but aluminum (1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p¹) loses a 3p electron. A 3p electron is higher in energy than a 3s electron and is partly shielded by the 3s electrons, so although aluminum has one more proton, its 3p electron is held less tightly and less energy removes it.
